title: People share a FlowWeb business with roles (owner, admin, helper, viewer), for the whole business or one flow, and each business sees only its own data
description: The Owner wants to give FlowWeb to friends and add people to a business or a single flow, to help out or just watch. Today flowweb.app lets in one hand-filled list of owner emails (fw_owners) and every mirrored row, machine and queued request sits in shared tables with no owner column, so a second person would see everything or nothing. Migration 0006 adds accounts (businesses), members with a role (owner: everything; admin: people, machines, flow controls, drafts; helper: works drafts; viewer: reads only), optionally limited to named flows (helper or viewer only), and invite links (for one email or anyone holding the link; used, revoked and expired ones fail). account_id goes on fw_mirror, fw_runners and fw_requests; row level security reads by membership and flow; every write is a SECURITY DEFINER function that checks the role; a machine token belongs to one business, so a relay only replaces and takes its own business's rows. Existing data moves into one business owned by the fw_owners logins, and the existing relay token keeps working. hosted/server/accounts.mjs holds the same role table for the screens. The hosted /v1 adds the account, member and invite routes and reads only the business the person chose (x-fw-account) or their only one. The migration is a production schema change: the Owner runs it.
acceptance: Migration 0006 runs after 0001-0005 and moves existing data into one business owned by the fw_owners logins; the old relay token keeps working
A stranger reads no mirror rows, machines, members or requests, and can make a business of their own
An email invite cannot be used by another email; a used or revoked invite fails; invites never make owners, and only helpers and viewers can be limited to flows
A whole-business viewer reads every mirror row; a one-flow viewer reads only that flow's rows; only owners and admins read machines and invites
Queued requests follow role and flow: helpers ask only draft changes, viewers ask nothing, one-flow members only for their flows
A relay snapshot or take never touches another business's rows
Admins cannot change or make owners, the last owner cannot step down or leave, anyone else can leave, only owners delete a business
hosted/server/accounts.mjs can(role, action) agrees with the database for every role and action

The hosted /v1 serves the account, member and invite routes, scopes mirror reads and machine and request calls to the chosen business, refuses a business the person is not in, and still answers /v1/session for a login with no business
